problem: Existing LLM-core VLN agents summarize navigation history with extra VLM+LLM calls, which adds noise, cost and latency. They also rely on fixed standard prompting rules, which limits the diversity of navigation strategies.
motivation: Objects, room type and orientation are the key information for VLN, yet text-summary memories lose or distort them. Humans use different strategies for different scenarios (e.g., recognizable kitchen vs. ambiguous utility room), so a fixed prescribed reasoning process is too rigid. Human-annotated VLN training paths can be turned into case-by-case demonstrations.
key_idea: Use a textual topological memory map (viewpoints, objects, object clusters) as both memory and global action space, and prompt the LLM with a retrieved human-path demonstration whose reasoning chain was mined by an LLM (Navigation Chain of Thought).
insight: The demonstration must be relevant and complete to help. Retrieving by instruction similarity gave no gain (SR 17 vs 18 with no demo), while retrieval by destination room type gave SR 23 with a full-step chain. A single-step example gave only SR 19, so the complete chain matters. Using GT room type gave SR 25 vs 23 with regex extraction, so cheap room-type parsing loses little.
method: Memory Topological Map: nodes are observed viewpoints (visited and unvisited), edges are mutual navigability, and the graph serves as the global action space; it is updated incrementally each step.
Perception to text: Faster R-CNN (Visual Genome) detects objects per viewpoint, and InstructBLIP-13B captions neighboring viewpoints only, prompted with the detected objects as context.

Object mapping and clustering: objects seen at one viewpoint are placed there, and objects seen in several viewpoints go to their geometric center. K-Means clusters nearby objects to hint at room type, and the map is serialized with a text template of cluster IDs, objects, and viewpoint IDs with captions and cluster relations.

CoT Mining: one training example per destination room type (27 in total) is sampled. The LLM plays the annotator and explains each GT viewpoint/object selection step by step, giving an instruction-path-explanation example set.
CoT Querying: the first room-type noun is parsed from the instruction by regex, encoded with Sentence-BERT, and the example with the highest cosine similarity is retrieved as the demonstration.

Prompt Manager: a prefix prompt (task role, I/O format, reasoning sub-tasks such as referring expression and exploration) plus an input prompt (instruction, map text, demo) is fed to the LLM, which selects a viewpoint and object.
Action: a shortest-path planner moves the agent to the selected map viewpoint.

setting.backbone: GPT-3.5-turbo-1106 and GPT-4o (frozen) as the navigator; Faster R-CNN and InstructBLIP-13B for perception; Sentence-BERT for retrieval
setting.training_data: none (training-free); a 27-example CoT set is drawn from the REVERIE training set (one per room type) and LLM-annotated
setting.observation: panoramic discrete views from the Matterport3D simulator, converted to object detections and captions
setting.action_space: discrete global nav-graph viewpoints (all observed viewpoints in the topological map) plus STOP
setting.privileged: none (GT room type is used only in an ablation); object proposals are provided by the REVERIE benchmark

numbers.extra: training-free; 27 CoT demos mined from the training set

numbers_note: The ablation LLM is not stated explicitly and is assumed to be GPT-3.5.
results: On the full REVERIE val-unseen split, training-free MC-GPT (SR 19.43, OSR 30.25) beats the training-based baselines (best FAST-MATTN SR 14.4), but trails the pre-trained models (DUET SR 46.98). On a 72-scene R2R subset with GPT-3.5 it beats NavGPT and MapGPT (SR 22.1 vs 19.4, NE 7.76 vs 8.48). With GPT-4o it gets a higher OSR (68.8) and lower NE (5.42) than MapGPT-GPT-4, but a lower SR (32.1 vs 41.2).
limitations: Far below pre-trained supervised VLN models on REVERIE (SR 19.43 vs DUET 46.98), and GPT-4o SR is below MapGPT-GPT-4.
VLM captioning hallucinates, and errors in detection and captioning propagate into the map.
R2R is evaluated only on a subset, and the ablations use just 100 REVERIE episodes; retrieval relies on a crude regex room-type parse.
